messages:
jamie: Hey team :wave: quick FYI before I hand off — noticed a pattern of short afternoon spikes on pool-alpha today, looks like small eval jobs are landing around 15:10-15:30 PT and causing burst throttles. Putting a proposed smoothing plan below.

priya: Thanks — can you paste the metrics snapshot?

jamie: sure. pasted from grafana at 15:05 PT: 
`pool-alpha utilization: 72% (5m avg)`
`burst available: 14 GPUs`
`queued jobs: 9 (avg runtime 3m)`
`throttle count: 8 at 15:12`

alex: hmmm okay. Those queued jobs are mostly cron-evals right?

jamie: yeah, 6/9 are nightly eval cron runs (small batch). The rest are ad-hoc dev jobs.

chen: Proposal: temporarily stagger the cron-evals by 10m windows (3 groups) for tonight and tomorrow morning to flatten the peaks. Also enable soft-preempt for ad-hoc low-priority jobs so they yield to reserved traffic.

marisol: +1 on stagger. Can we auto-detect when pool-alpha >75% and delay cron starts by X minutes?

jamie: we can. I sketched a tiny check in the cron controller: 
```
if pool_util > 0.75: sleep(rand_between(600, 1800))
else: run()
```
Would add jitter to avoid synchronized retries.

oncall-bot: Reminder: nightly-cache-prune job scheduled at 23:00 PT (team: eng-ml).

priya: If we add the pool check, please don't block the scheduled cache-prune — that's high priority.

alex: On soft-preempt — runtime already supports it but default priority for dev is 'normal'. We can push a quick change to mark cron-evals as 'low' so they get preempted automatically; will do a PR now. @chen can you make the cron controller change?

chen: Yep. I'll open a tiny PR to add the util check + jitter and a feature flag `crons.stagger_on_high_util=true`. Will add rollout to dev first.

jamie: For tonight's handoff: I'm enabling the feature flag in staging and will monitor. If things look stable for 30m, I'll flip it for prod. Leaving a note in ops-runbook.

marisol: If throttles persist after staggering, next step is to bump burst limits for pool-alpha temporarily or re-route some evals to pool-beta. But that needs approval from infra ops (cost).

priya: Agreed. Also, please add an alert tweak: current alert is pool_util > 85% for 10m. Suggest adding a short-warning when util > 70% for 5m tagged as FYI to oncall so we can proactively delay crons.

alex: I'll patch the alert in alert-manager: new rule `pool_alpha_warning: util>0.7 for 5m` -> notify #eng-oncall with `severity: info`.

jamie: timeline: staging flag enable in 10m, will watch 30m, flip prod if stable. If anyone sees unexpected fallback/errors, ping here and escalate to paging policy.

chen: PR: https://git.internal/r/2345 (adds check + flag). Diff is tiny.

marisol: Thanks. One more thing — there's a legacy cron that still targets pool-alpha directly (no flag). I can run a grep and open a follow-up ticket to migrate it.

jamie: awesome. handoff complete for my shift — @priya you're on for the next 6h. I'll be reachable for 30m for questions. :thumbsup:

priya: Got it. Thanks for the handoff and the plan. I'll monitor the new warning alerts.

oncall-bot: Deploy succeeded: cron-controller v1.12.3 -> canary on staging (15:22 PT).

alex: canary looks clean so far, no errors in controller logs.

priya: copied. Starting the 30m watch. If we hit throttle >12 or queued >15, we'll open a swap with infra.

jamie: noted. leaving a short checklist in the runbook: adjust alert -> enable flag -> monitor -> flip -> migrate legacy cron.

chen: tagging the ticket: ENGINFRA-678.

marisol: :eyes: thanks all.
